
# Thread `fix-it`'s sidecar

This bottle is the sidecar of thread `fix-it`, in the `project` repo: its agent
runs in the thread's own bottle and reaches this one over ssh, for jobs that
want more room. Its repos are as they were when it was made, with the thread's
remotes: a push from here lands in the thread's lane, which the thread's bottle
pushes into too, so fetch and merge before you push, and a push refused as not
a fast-forward lost a race: fetch, merge, push again. It's scratch: a pause of
the thread deletes it and keeps nothing of it, so push what's worth keeping.
To hand the user a file or a directory from here, give them the command that
copies it to their current directory: `folio sidecar cp fix-it:<path> .`

## Snapshots and pauses

folio snapshots this thread: `/notes` (of a checkout, its `.git` and every
worktree of its, wherever it is, and of their files all but ignored ones), and
your conversation and memory. A pause takes a snapshot and deletes the bottle,
and a resume makes a new one from it. Anything outside them is gone: the
scratchpad, the rest of `/tmp` and your home, installed packages, running
processes. So is anything they ignore.

Before a snapshot, folio asks you to get ready: an event from the `snapshot`
address (`from="snapshot~..."`) that starts "Snapshot interrupt". It's folio's,
part of how this bottle works, and expected: act on it as you would the user's
request. When one comes, finish or stop what you're doing, then:

1. Save what you'd want after a resume, above all what's only in your context:
   write it to `/notes`, commit and push, here and in `/notes`.
2. Look at what the snapshot will hold: large untracked files in the
   checkouts that you don't need (data, downloads, builds outside ignored
   paths), delete or ignore them. The event says how big the last snapshot was.
   Leave caches outside the checkouts as they are: they aren't snapshotted.
3. Reply with the send tool, to its from, the text `snapshot`. The snapshot is
   taken when you reply, so reply only once you're ready, and only once.

If the user is pausing, the pause waits for your reply. If Claude isn't running,
or the user forces it, folio snapshots without asking, so keep your notes and
pushes current anyway.

Keep only throwaway files outside them. Work in any other clone is committed
and pushed to `agent` as you go, on a `genie/` branch like any other, or it's
lost.

## Your sidecar

`ssh sidecar` reaches this thread's sidecar: a bottle of its own on runner `box`,
with 2G of memory and features none, for the jobs that want more
than this bottle has: builds, test suites, anything long or big. It's you
there, as `genie`, in a shell or with a command; scp and git over ssh work too.

- It has this bottle's repos at the same paths, as they were when it was made,
  with the same remotes: a push from there lands in this thread's lane, as one
  from here does. Two checkouts writing one lane share it as two people share a
  remote: a push refused as not a fast-forward lost a race, so fetch `agent`,
  merge, and push again. Work there on a branch of its own (the next
  `genie/<feature>-N`), so that the two rarely race.
- `/notes` there is a second checkout of these notes: commit there only what
  you find there, then `git pull agent main` before you push, there and here.
- Your work gets there over ssh, committed or not:
  `git push sidecar:/workspace $(git stash create || git rev-parse HEAD):refs/heads/job`,
  then `ssh sidecar 'cd /workspace && git checkout -q --detach job && ...'`.
- It's scratch: a pause deletes it and keeps nothing of it, and a resume makes
  a new one. Push what's worth keeping before then, from there or from here.
